gaps.sentence: I'd like ___ more time to think about your offer.
gaps.explanation: 'A little more time' means a small additional amount; 'time' is uncountable so 'a few' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: She gave the children two sweets ___.
gaps.hint: distribution per child at the end of the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'Two sweets each' means two per child; 'every' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: The hotel was full, so we had to look for ___ hotel.
gaps.explanation: 'Another hotel' means some other, unspecified one; 'the other hotel' would imply exactly two known hotels.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.

gaps.sentence: There is ___ milk in the fridge — help yourself.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement; the invitation confirms it
gaps.explanation: 'Some milk' fits the affirmative statement and the invitation; 'no milk' would contradict 'help yourself'.

gaps.sentence: The hall was so crowded that ___ found a seat.
gaps.hint: a crowded hall means no one succeeded
gaps.explanation: 'So crowded that nobody found a seat' matches the logic of the sentence; 'anybody' cannot be the subject of an affirmative clause.

gaps.sentence: I don't like ___ of these two paintings.
gaps.explanation: After 'don't like', 'either' is used: 'not ... either of them' means zero of the two; 'neither' would double the negative.
